questions.question: What major economic policy shift took place in India around 1991 regarding foreign trade and investment?
options: The government nationalised all foreign-owned private factories
The government removed trade barriers and restrictions on foreign investment, allowing goods to be imported and exported easily (Liberalisation)
India completely withdrew from international sea trade
A 200% tariff was levied on all foreign industrial machinery
questions.explanation: Around 1991, far reaching changes in policy were made in India. The government decided that the time had come for Indian producers to compete with producers around the globe. Removing barriers or restrictions set by the government is what is known as liberalisation.

questions.question: Why did Central and State governments in India set up Special Economic Zones (SEZs) with world-class facilities and tax exemptions?
options: To resettle displaced rural artisans in government handloom communes
To restrict multinational companies from selling products in Indian markets
To ban the use of modern internet technologies in factory operations
To attract foreign companies to invest in India by offering world-class infrastructure and exemption from taxes for an initial period of five years
questions.explanation: In recent years, the central and state governments in India are taking special steps to attract foreign companies to invest in India. Industrial zones, called Special Economic Zones (SEZs), are being set up with world class facilities (electricity, water, roads, transport). Companies who set up production units in the SEZs do not have to pay taxes for an initial period of five years.

questions.question: What is the primary stated objective of the World Trade Organisation (WTO)?
options: To set uniform minimum wage rates across all sovereign nations
To provide direct military defense to developing nations
To liberalise international trade and establish rules regarding international trade among member nations
To issue international currency notes replacing the US dollar
questions.explanation: World Trade Organisation (WTO) is an organisation whose aim is to liberalise international trade. Started at the initiative of developed countries, WTO establishes rules regarding international trade, and sees that these rules are obeyed.

questions.subtopic: Spreading of Production by an MNC
questions.question: In the NCERT example of an MNC manufacturing industrial equipment: the product is designed in the United States, parts are manufactured in China, and customer care is handled in India. Why is India preferred for customer care?
options: Because telephone calls are legally prohibited in other countries
Because India has no domestic industrial manufacturing factories
Because India has skilled, English-speaking youth and trained engineers available at competitive wage costs
Because customer care can only operate in tropical climates
questions.explanation: India has highly skilled engineers who can understand the technical aspects of production. It also has educated English speaking youth who can provide customer care services. And all this probably can mean 50-60 percent cost savings for the MNC.

questions.question: 'Foreign Investment' is defined as:
options: Gold coins purchased by ordinary domestic citizens in retail jewelry shops
Investment made by Multinational Corporations (MNCs) in physical assets like land, buildings, machines, and other equipment in another country
Loans provided by the central government to local village panchayats
Taxes paid by domestic retail shops to municipal corporations
questions.explanation: Money that is spent to buy assets such as land, building, machines and other equipment is called investment. Investment made by MNCs is called foreign investment. Any investment is made with the hope that these assets will earn profits.

questions.subtopic: Most Common Route for MNC Investment
questions.question: What is the most common route chosen by MNCs to establish and expand production in developing countries?
options: To construct brand new factories in deep uninhabited forests
To donate all manufacturing blueprints to municipal libraries
To buy up established local domestic companies and then expand their production network
To operate exclusively through postal money order catalog sales
questions.explanation: The most common route for MNC investments is to buy up local companies and then to expand production. MNCs with huge wealth can quite easily do so. For example, Cargill Foods, a very large American MNC, bought over Parakh Foods in India.

questions.subtopic: Example: Cargill Foods and Parakh Foods
questions.question: When American agribusiness giant Cargill Foods bought Parakh Foods in India, what valuable domestic asset did Cargill immediately acquire?
options: The entire sovereign fleet of the Indian Navy
Parakh Foods' extensive marketing network across India, well-known brand reputation, and five modern oil refineries
Exclusive mineral mining licenses in the Himalayas
The direct ownership of the Reserve Bank of India
questions.explanation: Parakh Foods had built a large marketing network in various parts of India, where its brand was well-reputed. Also, Parakh Foods had four oil refineries, whose control now shifted to Cargill. Cargill became the largest producer of edible oil in India.

questions.question: In industries like garments, footwear, and sports goods, how do large MNCs typically control production across developing nations?
options: They place orders with thousands of small decentralized local producers worldwide and sell the finished products under their own powerful brand names
They hire foreign armies to operate sewing machines in village workshops
They manufacture 100% of all garments in automated factories in Europe
They purchase raw cotton and burn it to raise global clothing prices
questions.explanation: Large MNCs in developed countries place orders for production with small producers. Garments, footwear, sports items are examples of industries where production is carried out by a large number of small producers around the world. The MNCs sell these under their own brand names.
